title: Tenant quarantine + slab recomposer runtime patch to stop ephemeral GPU OOM cascades
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Multiple customers (hosted, Dedicated and Private installs) experienced cascading GPU OOMs during bursty long-context inference windows. Investigation shows a correlated sequence: aggressive prefix caching + tenant handoff churn exposes a KV-index partial-commit path that leaves tombstones and tiny free slices in the GPU allocator's ephemeral arenas. Under burst load this produces an eviction storm and prevents allocation of large contiguous blocks needed for attention KV buffers, resulting in OOMs and long tail latency spikes. Scope: reported in three production incidents (2 hosted customers, 1 dedicated customer, 1 on-prem private deploy) across both Ampere and Hopper-based nodes. Impact: request failures, token truncation, degraded throughput, and 2 customer escalations to SE/CS teams. Goal: ship a runtime patch that halts the cascade immediately and prevents recurrence by repairing allocator fragmentation and closing the KV metadata leak path.
reproduction_steps: 1) Start a tenant-saturated workload that creates many short-lived chat sessions (prefix caching enabled, shared KV cache).
2) Trigger rapid session handoff (concurrent session migration + autoscale events), simulating burst traffic from multiple clients for ~10 minutes.
3) Observe allocator free-list splitting and accumulation of <64KB free fragments; KV index registers tombstones when partial commit happens during handoff.
4) Send long-context generation requests (>= 4096 tokens) that require contiguous KV buffers allocation and watch for OOMs and eviction storms.
mitigation_actions: Applied immediate tenant-level throttles for affected customers (limit concurrent sessions) to stop new allocation pressure.
Rolled an emergency config to reduce max sequence length for ephemeral workers in affected pool as a short-term workaround.
Scheduled rolling restarts for the 5 most pressured nodes to reclaim fragmented arenas (manual eviction + restart).
Opened customer-facing incidents and provided regression mitigations and ETA for fix.
proposed_fix_summary: Implement a 'slab recomposer' that runs in the runtime allocator to coalesce adjacent small free slices into larger contiguous blocks, add a tenant quarantine mode that prevents new heavy allocations while background compaction runs, and harden the KV-index commit path with an atomic reconcile step and tombstone compactor to prevent metadata leaks during session handoff.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR to feature branch + unit tests covering corner-case free-list states.
2) Canary build on non-prod GPU cluster for 24 hours with synthetic workload replay of reproduction steps.
3) Gradual 10% -> 30% -> 100% roll out in hosted pools with automatic rollback on >2x increasing OOM rate or >10% latency regression.
4) For Dedicated/Private customers provide opt-in patch package and assist with one-off canary runs; include manual rollback instructions.
5) Post-rollout: increase fragmentation/contiguity monitoring retention and schedule postmortem.
